title: Supercuspidal Representation Attached to a Datum
body_html:
Supercuspidal Representation Attached to a Datum

Let \(\Sigma=(x,\Gamma,\phi,\rho)\) be a supercuspidal datum and choose a good factorization of \(\Gamma\). The construction defines compact subgroups \[ K^i,\qquad K_{0+}^i,\qquad K_+^i \] from the Moy-Prasad groups of the Levi sequence \(G^i\). The character \(\phi\) extends to \(G_x^0K_+\), and the positive-depth factors produce a canonical irreducible representation \(\kappa\) of \(K=K^d\) whose restriction to \(K_+\) is \(\Gamma\)-isotypic.

The \(K\)-type attached to \(\Sigma\) is \[ \eta_\Sigma=\rho\otimes\kappa, \] where \(\rho\) is inflated from \(G_x^0/G_{x,0+}^0\). The representation attached to the datum is the compact induction \[ \pi_\Sigma=\operatorname{c-Ind}_{K}^{G}\eta_\Sigma. \] Under the paper's large residual characteristic hypotheses, Yu's construction and Kim's exhaustion theorem identify these representations with the tame supercuspidal representations of \(G\).
